title: Captured lesson
description: Plan 2.3 and 8. A reusable lesson tied to a real failure, a real correction or a surprising review result. The trigger vocabulary admits only those three, and both the trigger and the lesson carry mandatory evidence, so a run that simply ended cannot produce one: no manufactured lesson just because a run finished (release scenario 23). Supersession is recorded rather than overwritten — 'supersedes' on the envelope and 'superseded_by' here keep the chain readable in both directions, and a retired lesson keeps its history (plan 2.3, 8). Publication is a separate act from capture: ship may create a candidate, but publishing needs explicit authorization or a charter grant for KB publication and never treats 'ship happened' as permission to rewrite project knowledge (plan 7.1). The opt-in learning runtime reaches this artifact only as a candidate draft, whatever its ledger calls the lesson (ruling learning-drafts-not-publishes). Rolling back a skill revision leaves this artifact and its evidence untouched (release scenario 24).

status.description: 'candidate' is captured but unpublished; 'published' is in the KB; 'superseded' has been replaced and says by what; 'retired' no longer applies and says why. None of these deletes anything.

statement.description: The reusable lesson, stated so it can be applied to a future change rather than only recognised in this one.

trigger.description: Plan 2.3: a lesson exists because something went wrong, was corrected, or surprised a reviewer. There is no 'run-completed' member, and 'occurrence' binds the lesson to the artifact where it actually happened (release scenario 23).

occurrence.description: The finding, verification, review, event or ticket where it happened, bound by hash.

evidence.description: Revision-bound evidence for the lesson: the code, the receipt, the finding or the transcript that shows it is real. A lesson with no evidence is an opinion (plan 2.3).

applies_to.description: Where the lesson is relevant. Both fields are searchable by the learnings review lane, which is how an existing lesson gets reused instead of duplicated (plan 9 milestone 5).

guidance.description: What to do differently next time, concrete enough to act on.

counter_examples.description: Where the lesson does not apply. Kept so a lesson does not grow into a universal rule it was never evidence for.

superseded_by.description: The lesson that replaces this one. The replacement's envelope 'supersedes' points back, so the chain reads in both directions and no provenance is silently erased (plan 2.3).

supersession.description: Why the change happened. compound-refresh keeps, updates, consolidates, replaces or retires a lesson, and records the evidence for whichever it did (plan 2.3).

related.description: Existing lessons on the same ground. Checked before capture so an existing lesson is reused rather than duplicated (plan 9 milestone 5).

publication.description: Plan 7.1 and 8. Publishing to the KB is authorized separately from capturing: either a human asked for it, or a charter grant covers KB publication. A completed ship is not itself permission, and it is not permission to rewrite project knowledge (ruling `central-kb-owns-project-artifacts`). The central knowledgebase owns this artifact: `kb_ref` is deliberately a free locator rather than common#/$defs/repo_path, so a published lesson cannot name an application-local documentation tree as its home. Directory names under the knowledgebase root are configurable; the central ownership is not.

skill_changes.description: Skill revisions this lesson motivated. writing-skills can turn a supported lesson into a candidate skill change, but promotion requires evaluation and a separate review (plan 8). A rolled-back skill revision does not roll back the lesson: this artifact, its evidence and its supersession chain survive the rollback intact (release scenario 24), which is why 'rolled_back' is recorded here rather than expressed by deleting anything.

allOf.description: Promotion requires both the evaluation and the separate review (plan 8).
A published lesson carries its publication authorization. Capture alone never publishes (plan 7.1).
A superseded lesson names its replacement and records why. Silently erasing provenance is the failure this prevents (plan 2.3).
A retired lesson records the retirement and its evidence. Retirement is a recorded state, not a deletion (plan 2.3, release scenario 24).
A consolidation names the lessons it absorbed, so the originals stay findable (plan 2.3).
